editorial:
Imagine traveling back to Barcelona in 1913, where everyone is stiff and terrified of talking about sex. You get dropped right into a world where a quirky doctor tries to use Freud's new ideas to solve a mystery. It feels like a funny version of Sherlock Holmes, but instead of searching for clues in the street, the characters are digging through their own dreams and hidden desires. The vibe is lighthearted and a bit cheeky, making you laugh at how awkward people were back then while they tried to figure out why they felt certain ways about their partners.

What really works here is the chemistry between the leads and the way the mystery unfolds without feeling too heavy. The pacing stays snappy, though some of the slow-burn romance might feel a bit long for some. If you enjoy stories that poke fun at old-school rules, you will love this. Since it looks so beautiful, you should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you can. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move to catch all those colorful city details.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when the main characters finally stop lying to themselves about their feelings. After a series of funny misunderstandings, the mystery is solved not through a big crime, but through emotional honesty. The final twist reveals that the secrets everyone was hiding were much simpler than they thought. They realize that letting go of shame is the only way to find real happiness, and the movie ends with a sweet, romantic resolution.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky mysteries and romantic comedies set in the past.
